hook.en: Shareholders, workers, customers and the government all expect something from a company. Can one firm satisfy them all?
hook.kn: ಷೇರುದಾರರು, ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು, ಗ್ರಾಹಕರು ಮತ್ತು ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಎಲ್ಲರೂ ಕಂಪನಿಯಿಂದ ಏನನ್ನಾದರೂ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಒಂದು ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ಎಲ್ಲರನ್ನೂ ತೃಪ್ತಿಪಡಿಸಬಹುದೇ?

objectives.en: Name the four kinds of social responsibility
Explain responsibility towards shareholders, workers, consumers, government and community

narration.en: Shareholders, workers, customers and the government all expect something from a company. Can one firm satisfy them all?

body.en: Economic responsibility: produce goods and services that society wants and sell them at a profit. Legal responsibility: obey the laws of the land. Ethical responsibility: behave in ways society expects even when not written in law, such as respecting religious sentiments in advertisements. Discretionary responsibility: purely voluntary actions such as donations to educational institutions or help during floods.

points.en: Economic: produce what society wants, at a profit

narration.en: There are four kinds of social responsibility: economic, legal, ethical and discretionary.

title.en: On the board: Kinds of social responsibility

narration.en: Think of social responsibility as a pyramid. At the base is economic responsibility: make what society wants, at a profit.

say.en: Think of social responsibility as a pyramid. At the base is economic responsibility: make what society wants, at a profit.
Next, legal responsibility: obey the laws of the land.
Then ethical responsibility: behave as society expects even where no law says so, such as respecting religious feelings in ads.
At the top, discretionary responsibility: purely voluntary help, like donations for flood relief.
Business also has duties to each interest group.
Shareholders want a fair return, workers fair wages, consumers quality at fair prices, and the community taxes paid and a clean environment.

narration.en: Sort each action into the kind of social responsibility it shows.

explanation.en: Economic: produce and earn profit. Legal: obey the law. Ethical: do what society expects even beyond the law. Discretionary: purely voluntary help.

text.en: Making good-quality goods people want and selling them at a profit
Earning enough to survive and grow
Paying taxes and following labour laws
Following food safety rules on labels
Not hurting religious feelings in an advertisement
Not overcharging in a shortage, though no law forbids it
Donating a library to a government school

body.en: Towards shareholders: a fair and regular return, safety of investment, and accurate information about the company. Towards workers: fair wages, good working conditions, and respect for their right to form unions. Towards consumers: right quality and quantity at reasonable prices, no adulteration, no misleading advertising, and after-sales service. Towards government and community: obey laws, pay taxes honestly, protect the environment and act as a good citizen.
body.kn: ವ್ಯವಹಾರವು ಷೇರುದಾರರಿಗೆ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲ, ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರಿಗೆ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ವೇತನ, ಗ್ರಾಹಕರಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಾಮಾಣಿಕ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮತ್ತು ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಮುದಾಯಕ್ಕೆ ಉತ್ತಮ ಪೌರತ್ವ ನೀಡಬೇಕು.

points.en: Consumers: quality, fair price, honest advertising
Government and community: laws, taxes, environment

narration.en: A business owes a fair return to shareholders, fair wages to workers, honest dealing to consumers, and good citizenship to the government and community.

body.en: Economic, Legal, Ethical, Discretionary: Every Law Expects Decency. The first two are required, ethical is expected, discretionary is purely voluntary.

narration.en: Remember: Every Law Expects Decency. Economic, Legal, Ethical, Discretionary. The last one, discretionary, is purely voluntary.

problem.en: Classify each action by the kind of social responsibility: (a) A biscuit maker pays GST on time. (b) A firm donates ₹5 lakh to flood relief in Kodagu. (c) An advertiser avoids an advert that could hurt religious feelings, though no law forbids it.

steps.en: (a) Paying GST is required by law: legal responsibility.
(b) A donation is purely voluntary: discretionary responsibility.
(c) Behaviour society expects but law does not require: ethical responsibility.
